description: Manage the run lifecycle, ownership epoch and recorded decision boundary.

commands.usage:
usage: orchid run start
Acquire a fresh ownership epoch for initialized state; prints the epoch. This does not plan or dispatch work.

usage: orchid run resume
Fence a fresh ownership epoch after checking that the previous interactive session or supervisor has ended. Then reconcile jobs and load context before continuing.

usage: orchid run refresh-lease
Refresh the current run lease. The active orchestrator owns this routine maintenance.

usage: orchid run release-lease
Release this session's lease under its valid ORCHID_EPOCH; use after its final action.

usage: orchid run boundary show
Read the recorded decision boundary. Raw exit 16 means a boundary is present; exit 0 means none. This view does not clear or settle it.

usage: orchid run boundary set --kind <kind> [--task <id>] --reason "<reason>" [--no-count]
Record a fenced, journaled decision boundary. Kinds: planning, blocked-task, review-evidence, review-conflict, hook-failure, worktree-conflict, operator-handoff, task-prerequisite, run-complete, operator-decision. --no-count records without spending a model wakeup.

usage: orchid run boundary clear --reason "<reason>"
Clear the recorded boundary under a valid epoch after its condition has been resolved. An absent boundary is a successful no-op; clearing the record does not perform the prerequisite or acceptance work.
examples: ORCHID_REPO=<repo> ORCHID_EPOCH=<epoch> orchid run boundary clear --reason "<resolution>"

commands.usage:
usage: orchid run advance <status> --reason "<reason>"
Record a legal run-state transition under a valid epoch. Statuses are planning, running, accepting, blocked, complete; complete can only be reached through run accept with evidence. Illegal transitions retain raw exit 3. Requesting the current non-complete state is a successful no-op.

usage: orchid run accept --reason "<reason>" --evidence <file>
Accept only a run in accepting state. A readable acceptance evidence file and operator decision are required; this is the sole path to complete.
examples: ORCHID_REPO=<repo> ORCHID_EPOCH=<epoch> orchid run accept --reason "<acceptance decision>" --evidence <file>

commands.usage:
usage: orchid run new --reason "<reason>"
Archive a complete or blocked run and begin fresh planning while carrying context and active lessons. Requires a valid epoch and no live orchestrator lease; never use this to resume an active run.
examples: ORCHID_REPO=<repo> ORCHID_EPOCH=<epoch> orchid run new --reason "<new run goal>"
